loci.name: code-verbal-calibration-occupied-or-open
loci.one_line: Is 'execution-grounded train-time calibration of EXPRESSED confidence for code' genuinely unoccupied, or does RLCM's OOD LiveCodeBench result / Functional Entropy / Rewarding Doubt already collapse it to 'X but for code'?
loci.rationale: THE novelty gate (P1). If RLCM's math-trained hidden-state probe already achieves best accuracy+calibration on LiveCodeBench and is trivially decodable to text, a code-verbalization paper is derivative. Investigator must pull RLCM's exact LiveCodeBench numbers, determine whether its probe is distinct from a trained self-report, and fold in the Campos multicalibration-for-code competitor check (does its skill-score gain reflect discrimination or just calibration/threshold relocation — it never reports AUROC). Output: a crisp novelty-defense or a pivot.

loci.name: collapse-proof-training-objective
loci.one_line: Which exact train-time objective for expressed code-confidence provably avoids the disconnect paper's 'calibration without discrimination' collapse AND the DCPO gradient-conflict?
loci.rationale: THE confidence gate (P2). The paper's own SFT collapsed (274 ex, coarse tiers, joint objective). Fight: 260113284 says RLVR worsens overconfidence / SFT calibrates better; DCPO proves a gradient conflict jointly optimizing accuracy+calibration; against this, CAPO (discrimination-first surrogate), Beyond-Binary-Rewards (proper scoring rule), ORCE (decoupled confidence head), Rewarding Doubt (log-score RL, single-GPU) all show clean AUROC 0.79-0.86 — but all QA. Investigator picks the objective+architecture most likely to make code self-report DISCRIMINATE, with the mechanism for why it beats collapse.

loci.name: self-report-vs-external-judge-vs-probe-reversal
loci.one_line: Given AutoProbe's validated three-way reversal (self-report fails everywhere; external LLM-judge wins on simple code 0.94; internal probe wins on repo-level 0.82), should the method train the coder's own self-report, a decoupled estimator, or route by complexity?
loci.rationale: Decides the METHOD's architecture and whether the alternative Direction D (complexity-conditional routing) is worth a section or is the headline. Reconciles our paper's 'verbal fails 0.52' (self-assessment) with AutoProbe's 'judge 0.94' (external, simple code). Determines if training the coder's OWN token-level self-report can beat the external-judge ceiling — the crux of an expressed-interface contribution.

loci.name: label-and-data-feasibility
loci.one_line: On single-GPU 7B compute and a tight timeline, which label mechanism (zero-sample proper-scoring vs N=100 MC-sample vs K-sample DPO) and how many code problems are needed to train discriminative confidence without repeating the 274-example collapse?
loci.rationale: Pure feasibility gate (P2 / 'don't waste time & money'). ConfTuner needs 0 sampling for labels; Uncertainty Distillation needs ~100 samples/question; ORCE needs K/prompt. The execution-pass-rate label our paper already computes (n=10) is a natural cheap-ish target. Investigator estimates GPU-hours to build labels + train on HumanEval+MBPP+LiveCodeBench (+ synthetic problems if needed), flags the Cohere 'verification ceiling' risk for LLM-generated tests, and confirms the plan fits single-GPU.

loci.name: fallback-utility-of-collapsed-confidence
loci.one_line: If the train-time intervention only partially breaks the collapse, does the (still-calibrated) signal retain downstream utility via risk-controlled selective generation, giving a defensible secondary headline?
loci.rationale: Serves the query's MANDATORY 'failure mode + pre-registered fallback.' Establishes a floor: even if verbal discrimination lands short of the 0.85 target, a risk-coverage / selective-generation headline (CIC conformal abstention wrapper on the trained signal, or pivot to execution-based Task Abstention) keeps the paper alive. This is the anti-dead-paper insurance.
